submission.hypothesis: The locked Python graph expanded from 9 to 34 packages because the Host distribution (ordivon-host) directly depends on `mcp==2.0.0` and, transitively, `ordivon-protocol` (pinned to a Computing git commit) plus the `anc_*` packages (anc_canonical, anc_effect_ir, anc_effect_binding, anc_tool_contract) imported by the code-change Host, and the mcp SDK/starlette/pydantic HTTP stack that mcp_server.py imports. The single causal owner is `pyproject.toml`'s unconditional `[project.dependencies]` list, which makes every consumer of `ordivon-host` (both the CLI workload surface and the MCP server surface) install the entire server-side dependency graph even for pure CLI/World-core use.
submission.causalMechanism: pyproject.toml declares runtime `dependencies = ["mcp==2.0.0", "ordivon-protocol @ git+..."]` with no optional/extra separation and no `[project.optional-dependencies]` gate for the MCP server surface. `src/ordivon_host/mcp_server.py` imports `mcp.server`, `mcp.server.transport_security`, `mcp.types`, pydantic, and starlette, so installing the ordivon-host wheel pulls the mcp SDK plus its pydantic/starlette ASGI transport stack. `src/ordivon_host/__init__.py` eagerly imports `McpRuntimeClient` from `.runtime`, and `src/ordivon_host/engine/code_change/host.py` imports the `anc_*` protocol packages, so the public package __init__ forces the ancestor/ordivon-protocol graph. The CLI entrypoint (`ordivon-host`) shares the same installed environment as the MCP server (`ordivon-host-mcp`) because both come from the same wheel and there is no extra that installs the server transport separately. Because the distribution carries the MCP server entrypoint `ordivon-host-mcp` as a first-class script and the SDK pins/exposes a large ASGI/starlette/pydantic stack, a World-core consumer doing a normal `pip/uv install ordivon-host` gains the full 34-package server graph even though it only needs the CLI/workload plane. The failure is not that the MCP server needs a server dependency — it legitimately does — but that the Host distribution does not isolate that server-only dependency set behind an extra, so a core-only consumer cannot install a lean graph and the distribution's locked graph is forced to 34.
submission.nextFalsifier: Split the MCP server surface into an optional extra (e.g. `ordivon-host[mcp-server]`) with `mcp==2.0.0` and the starlette/pydantic ASGI stack moved there, keep only the lean core dependencies in `[project.dependencies]`, and update `uv.lock` so a World core consumer `pip install ordivon-host` resolves the original ~9-package graph while `install ordivon-host[mcp-server]` yields the 34-package graph and the `ordivon-host-mcp` entrypoint still passes its full 44/44 Host semantics including the authenticated loopback MCP probe and six-Tool serverInterface receipt. The falsifier passes only if (a) the core-only lock resolves to the small graph, (b) the MCP extra still passes `ordivon-host-mcp --check`, the 2026-07-28 server/discover probe, and the exact six-Tool catalog, and (c) `ordivon_host/__init__.py` and the CLI entrypoint no longer force-import the mcp/starlette server stack so a World core consumer importing `ordivon_host` never loads the server transport.
